title: $NodeImport:$ Imbalanced Node Classification with Node Importance Assessment

problem.claim: Class imbalance in graph node classification causes majority classes to dominate training and biases model performance.

gap.claim: Existing approaches based on class size prioritization or minority-node synthesis do not effectively address class imbalance.

contributions.claim: NodeImport measures node importance using a balanced meta-set and selects nodes that improve performance under an unbiased setting.
The paper derives a formula for directly assessing node importance, reducing computational overhead and providing a threshold for node selection.
The framework filters valuable labeled, unlabeled, and synthetic nodes while separating synthetic-node generation from filtering.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe their approach and framework as novel for class-imbalanced node classification.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report evaluating NodeImport on multiple benchmark datasets with popular GNN architectures.
The authors report that NodeImport outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.
The authors report flexibility and effectiveness in mitigating class imbalance and improving node classification outcomes.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph node classification is challenged by class imbalance, which biases training toward majority classes.
Existing class-prioritization and node-synthesis approaches are described as insufficient.
NodeImport uses a balanced meta-set and performance-based importance assessment for dynamic node selection.
The method derives an importance formula, filters multiple node types, separates generation from filtering, and constructs a representative meta-set.
The authors report benchmark evaluation with popular GNN architectures and improved results over state-of-the-art baselines.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, metrics, quantitative gains, or baseline configurations.
The abstract does not provide the derived importance formula, threshold assumptions, or algorithmic complexity.
The abstract does not describe the construction procedure or exact distribution-matching criterion for the meta-set.
